dish.title: Potato and Leek Gratin
dish.description: Thinly sliced potatoes and leeks baked in a cream and cheese custard until the center is tender and the top is browned.

provenance.process: FlavorWeave Catalog Factory Dry Run #3, Grok Bot only

recipe_version.title: Potato and Leek Gratin
recipe_version.description: Thinly sliced potatoes and leeks baked in a cream and cheese custard until the center is tender and the top is browned.

ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes
ingredients.note: as purchased, then peeled. About 4 medium potatoes.

ingredients.name: leeks
ingredients.note: about 1 lb untrimmed. White and pale green only.
ingredients.preparation: halved, rinsed, and sliced 1/4 inch thick

ingredients.name: heavy cream
ingredients.note: required dairy. All of it goes into the custard.

ingredients.name: vegetarian Gruyère
ingredients.note: required dairy. A block, grated by the cook, not a pre-shredded blend. Divided: 2 oz whisked into the cream, 2 oz on top. Microbial rennet so the vegetarian claim does not depend on a swap.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.note: required dairy. Divided: 1 tbsp to cook the leeks, 1 tbsp to grease the dish.

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: divided: 1/4 tsp on the leeks, 1 tsp in the custard

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.note: all of it in the custard

ingredients.name: ground nutmeg
ingredients.note: spice seed. Not a peanut and not a tree nut.

steps.title: Slice and grate
steps.body: Peel the Yukon Gold potatoes and slice them 1/8 inch thick. Hold the slices in cold water so they do not discolor. Trim the leeks to the white and pale green, halve them lengthwise, rinse out the grit, and slice them 1/4 inch thick. Grate the vegetarian Gruyère. Mince the garlic. Strip the fresh thyme leaves. This prep finishes before the oven is turned on.

steps.title: Heat the oven and soften the leeks
steps.body: Heat the oven to 400 F. The preheat takes about 10 minutes, and those 10 minutes are inside the cook time. During that same 10 minutes, melt 1 tbsp of the unsalted butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add the leeks and 1/4 tsp of the kosher salt. Cook until soft, about 8 minutes. Do not let them go dark brown. The leek cooking is inside the preheat and is not a second block of time.

steps.title: Mix the cream-cheese custard
steps.body: Whisk the heavy cream with 2 oz of the vegetarian Gruyère, the garlic, 1 tsp of the kosher salt, the black pepper, the ground nutmeg, and the fresh thyme. This cream-cheese custard is defined here from those ingredients. It is not a bottled sauce. There is no egg and no flour in it. The remaining 2 oz of cheese is for the top.

steps.title: Layer the dish
steps.body: Use the remaining 1 tbsp unsalted butter to grease a 2-quart baking dish. Drain the Yukon Gold potatoes and pat them dry. Layer the potatoes with the softened leeks, pouring the cream-cheese custard over the layers as you go. Press the slices down so the cream comes nearly to the top. Do not add milk, stock, or water that is not in the ingredient list. Scatter the remaining 2 oz vegetarian Gruyère over the top. Do not add breadcrumbs.

steps.title: Bake and rest
steps.body: Bake on the middle rack at 400 F for 40 minutes. A knife should meet little resistance in a center potato slice, the cream should be bubbling at the edges and look thickened, and the cheese on top should be browned in patches. If the top colors deeply before the 40 minutes are up, lay a loose piece of foil over the dish for the rest of that 40 minutes. Rest 5 minutes before serving. The 40-minute bake and the 5-minute rest come after the 10-minute preheat and are inside the cook time. There is no breadcrumb crust. kitchen_tested is false: 40 minutes is the expected bake for 1/8-inch slices, not a tested promise. If the center is still firm at 40 minutes, keep baking and check every 5 minutes; that extra time is not inside the 70-minute total.

recipe_version.heat: Oven 400 F. Leeks sauté over medium during the preheat. Bake on the middle rack.
recipe_version.doneness: Center potato slice takes a knife with little resistance. Cream is bubbling at the edges and thickened, not watery. Cheese on top is browned in patches. No breadcrumb crust. Rest 5 minutes. Written bake is 40 minutes at 400 F for 1/8-inch slices. kitchen_tested is false. Extra time beyond 40 minutes, if the center is still firm, is not included in the 70-minute total.

curator_preflight.detail: Every listed ingredient is used in a step. Cheese is split 2 oz in the custard and 2 oz on top. Butter is split 1 tbsp for the leeks and 1 tbsp for the dish. No breadcrumb is introduced in the method.
There is no oil. The fat is unsalted butter, 2 tbsp, divided and both parts used. Heavy cream is an ingredient in the custard, not a stand-in for the butter.
The cream-cheese custard is whisked from heavy cream, half the Gruyère, garlic, salt, pepper, nutmeg, and thyme. It is not a jar. No flour and no egg.

Prep 15 is slicing, rinsing, and grating, finished before the oven is on. Cook 55 is 10 minutes of preheat, 40 minutes of baking, and 5 minutes of rest. The leek sauté (about 8 minutes) runs inside the 10-minute preheat and is not added again. 15 + 55 = 70. An untested extra bake, if the center is still firm, is disclosed and is not inside the 70.
Base 4. Cream, cheese, and potatoes scale, with a cream floor and a smaller dish at 1 serving so the potatoes are not baked dry. Oven temperature does not scale. See scaling_notes.

scaling_notes.1: One serving is 8 oz Yukon Gold potatoes (about 1 medium potato), sliced 1/8 inch, not a handful of ends. Leek: the white and pale green of 1/2 leek. Cream floor: 1/2 cup heavy cream, which is the true quarter and is enough only in a small 2-cup baking dish; do not spread it across the 2-quart dish. Cheese: 1 oz vegetarian Gruyère, half whisked into the cream and half on top, not a dusting. Butter: 1 tsp total, half to soften the leek and half to grease the small dish. Garlic: 1 small clove, not a quarter clove. Salt: a pinch on the leek and 1/4 tsp in the custard. Pepper, nutmeg, and thyme: a quarter of the written amount (a scant pinch of nutmeg). Oven stays 400 F. Start checking at 30 minutes. The doneness test is the same: a tender center slice and thickened cream. Do not change the temperature to speed it up.
scaling_notes.2: 1 lb potatoes, 1 leek, 1 cup heavy cream, 2 oz vegetarian Gruyère (1 oz in the custard, 1 oz on top), 1 tbsp butter, 1 garlic clove. Use a 1-quart dish so the cream still comes nearly to the top of the slices. Halve the salt, pepper, nutmeg, and thyme. Same 400 F. Check at about 35 minutes; the written 40 minutes is for the full dish.
scaling_notes.4: As written. 2 lb potatoes, 2 cups heavy cream, 4 oz cheese, a 2-quart dish, 40 minutes at 400 F after a 10-minute preheat.
do_not_scale: dish size must shrink with the batch

HH001 cannot eat it. The clock is about 70 minutes, a different length and a different format from the planned pork braise and the planned stuffed cabbage.

Compared with Harissa Roasted Carrots with Feta: both are dairy, and that one is the live north-african roast with feta on carrots. This is potatoes and leeks in a cream custard, with no feta and no harissa. Compared with Lentil-Stuffed Cabbage (DR2, certified, unimplemented): both go in a baking dish, but that one is rolls in tomato sauce with no dairy. Compared with Cider-Braised Pork Shoulder (DR2): both run longer than the live 40-minute cluster, but that one is a meat braise. This is a vegetarian gratin.
